item.title: The Bank of England Has a Trump Problem as Iran War Blocks Rate Cuts
item.description: Read between the lines and the Bank of England has a simple message for British workers losing their jobs or homeowners facing high mortgage rates: Blame Donald Trump.

item.title: Blackstone Said to Buy $25 Billion HSBC Australia Home Loan Book
item.description: Blackstone Inc. has agreed to acquire an about A$36 billion ($25 billion) home loan portfolio in Australia from HSBC Holdings Plc, people familiar with the matter said, in what’s set to be one of the largest such transactions ever.

item.title: Womenswear Firm Reformation Opens Flat After $210.9 Million IPO
item.description: Reformation Inc., a sustainable womenswear brand backed by private equity firm Permira, opened at its IPO price in its trading debut Thursday, after the company raised $210.9 million in a listing that priced at the bottom of its marketed range.

item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix Answer AI Doubters With Big Numbers and Deals
item.description: In a remarkable week, the titans of the near-$1 trillion global memory industry smashed profit records. But they were unable to reverse a market rout that’s erased much of their stocks’ gains this year.

item.title: ‘Talk Is Cheap’: Wall Street Delivers Harsh Verdict on Warsh Fed
item.description: It had been just six weeks since Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh vowed to reestablish the central bank’s reputation as an inflation fighter. But as he took to the podium to explain why the Fed again sat on the fence Wednesday — and held interest rates steady even as consumer prices keep rising far faster than its target, month after month — Wall Street analysts found the message far from reassuring.

item.title: BOE’s Bailey Says Young Bear Brunt of Low Hire, Low Fire Economy
item.description: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that Britain’s static labor market is behind the surge in youth unemployment.

item.title: Equinix Seeks at Least $3 Billion From Latest Data Center Deal
item.description: Data center firm Equinix Inc. is looking to raise at least $3 billion from a sale of US investment-grade bonds, according to people familiar with the matter, selling into a recently weakened environment for debt related to the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Google Unveils Gemini AI for Robots Struggling With Dexterity
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google DeepMind unveiled a new artificial intelligence model for robots that allows humanoid machines to coordinate movements across their entire bodies, marking its latest effort to extend its Gemini AI technology to allow robots to reason, plan multi-step tasks and adapt to human environments.

item.title: Nigeria Central Bank Sees Transition to Inflation Target by 2028
item.description: Nigeria’s central bank said plans to shift to an inflation-targeting regime haven’t been derailed by price pressures emanating from the Iran war, and it expects to conclude the process in two years’ time.

item.title: Oracle (ORCL) Stock Jumps as Google Gemini AI Partnership Expands
item.description: Oracle Corp. gained more than 8% after saying it would expand a partnership with Google Cloud to bring Gemini artificial intelligence tools to its business customers.

item.title: Short Gilts Surge as Traders Slash Bets on BOE Hike in September
item.description: Short-dated UK government bonds had their biggest daily rally in more than a month after the Bank of England left interest rates unchanged and pointed to easing domestic inflationary pressures.

item.title: Yen Surge Spurs Speculation Japan Intervened in Market Again
item.description: The yen surged by 2% against the US dollar, marking its biggest jump since Japanese officials intervened in the market earlier this year.

item.title: Chile Finance Minister Floats Idea of Private Capital at Codelco
item.description: Chile’s right-wing government opened the door to bringing private capital into copper giant Codelco in a way that retains state control, the latest twist in a debate over the indebted company’s future.

item.title: Scale AI Names Google Cloud Executive Francis deSouza as New CEO
item.description: Scale AI Inc. has appointed an executive from Alphabet Inc.’s Google to be its first permanent chief executive officer in more than a year since Meta Platforms Inc. invested $14.3 billion in the data-labeling startup and hired away its CEO.

item.title: Iconiq Backs Satellite Startup K2 Space at $6.8 Billion Value
item.description: Startup K2 Space, which builds large satellites for high-power tasks like data-heavy communications and defense missions, has raised $500 million in a new round of funding, the company plans to announce Thursday.

item.title: Indian Air Force Seeks Local Makers as Wars Disrupt Supplies
item.description: Indian Air Force identified dozens of critical components it wants domestic manufacturers to produce after wars in Ukraine and the Middle East disrupted defense supply chains, as part of a broader effort to boost self-reliance in military production.

item.title: US GDP Growth Softens Despite Strong Consumer, Investment
item.description: US economic growth moderated in the second quarter, though a pickup in consumer spending and solid business investment signaled underlying strength.

item.title: Mexico Economy Rebounds More Than Expected in Second Quarter
item.description: Mexico’s economy rebounded in the second quarter after exports rose to a record despite prolonged trade tensions with the US.

item.title: Strategy Shores Up Liquidity as Bitcoin Faithful Wait on Rebound
item.description: After a five-week pause on Bitcoin purchases, Strategy Inc. investors are left wondering what’s next for the largest buyer of the cryptocurrency following a tumultuous period.

item.title: Goldman Traders Say Stocks Lack ‘Juice’ for Meaningful Breakout
item.description: For almost two months, investors have tried — and largely failed — to deduce a signal that would break US equities’ newfangled habit of lurching around and going nowhere.

item.title: Big Oil Is Making Big Money During Iran War Market Turmoil
item.description: Dislocations have created lucrative opportunities for companies able to source, transport and process energy across markets.

item.title: German Inflation Accelerates to Three-Month High on Energy
item.description: German inflation accelerated to the highest level in three months after temporary fuel-price relief expired and renewed fighting in the Middle East bolstered oil.

item.title: Meta Reports $279 Billion in Future Data Center Leases for AI
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. said it has $279 billion in future lease agreements mostly related to artificial intelligence data centers that are not yet reflected on its balance sheet.

item.title: A16z-Backed Biotech Braveheart Seeks $318.8 Million in US IPO
item.description: Braveheart Bio Inc., a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company backed by a16z, is seeking to raise as much as $318.8 million in an initial public offering, adding to a growing pipeline of listings in the sector.

item.title: US Stock Futures Today: Chipotle, Crocs, Meta, Microsoft, Starbucks
item.description: S&P 500 Index futures rise 0.7% as of 7:50 a.m. in New York as results from Microsoft boost sentiment for the tech sector.

item.title: European Banks Want a Slice of AI Profits, But Less of the Risk
item.description: Europe’s top banks want to earn more from the debt-fueled artificial intelligence boom, while seeking ways to limit and offset exposures to the red-hot sector.

item.title: US Stocks Rally With Boost From Microsoft’s Surge; Chips Jump
item.description: US stocks rose at the open on Thursday as Microsoft Corp. soared 16% after reporting the fastest cloud unit growth in four years. Top semiconductor companies, like Micron Technology Inc. and Nvidia Corp., gained as well.

item.title: Kenya Considers Debut Panda Bond to Diversify Funding Sources
item.description: Kenya is considering an inaugural yuan-denominated bond in China’s onshore debt market, according to people familiar with the plans, as the East African nation seeks to diversify its funding sources.

item.title: EU Pledges €10 Billion in Public Funding for New AI Data Centers
item.description: The European Union invited companies to apply to build as many as seven artificial intelligence data centers in Europe backed by public funds, furthering the bloc’s closely-watched plan to cut its reliance on overseas technology.

item.title: From Highest Levy to Duty-Free: Lesotho Lauds US Shift
item.description: Products from the tiny southern African mountain kingdom of Lesotho, which had endured the highest tariffs on any nation from the US, can now enter the world’s biggest economy duty-free.
